accuracy.reason: All eight objectives are accurately scoped: accepted versus ready, publisher versus consumer acknowledgement, transactional duplicate protection versus delivery, bounded retries/DLQ, ordered effects, finite buffering, independent log positions and completion-dependent sync decisions. All primary source claims and diagram meanings verified; no universal durability/order/exactly-once guarantee.

evidence.quote: That transaction protects its database effects. It does not make an external email or payment atomic, or turn delivery into a universal exactly-once guarantee.

mechanisms.reason: Traces successful handoff/effect/ack and both crash gaps, then closes the duplicate-credit gap with unique durable operation ID plus effect in one transaction. Wrong-last-write ordering, serialized per-entity effects, arrival-minus-completion growth and independent offsets provide concrete transferable causal explanations.

evidence.quote: In one database transaction, insert that ID into a durable processed-jobs table with a unique constraint and apply the job's database effect. Commit both or neither. A duplicate ID skips the effect. A separate check followed by a write can race or crash between steps.

coherence.reason: Actors and status precede redelivery, retries, ordering and capacity; queue-versus-log choice uses already-defined consumer work and duplicate effects. Final request-boundary decision integrates these costs. Both diagrams preserve acceptance/completion and shared-work/independent-history boundaries.

evidence.quote: These acknowledgements cover different boundaries. Neither makes a broker operation atomic with a database write or proves an arbitrary business effect succeeded.

decisions.reason: Makes deferred result/status/operating costs explicit, forbids premature access authorization, distinguishes temporary from invalid work and deliberate replay, limits downstream work and arrivals, and chooses retained groups only when independent history/replay is needed.

evidence.quote: More workers help when workers are the bottleneck and downstream services have spare capacity. If the database is already saturated, more workers increase contention instead.

clarity.reason: Terms are defined with actors and state transitions. Credit, address order and rate arithmetic illustrate different failure mechanisms without extraneous implementation detail. Kafka partition/offset/group terms are explained before their retention and ordering limits.

evidence.quote: In Kafka, a partition is an ordered slice of the log. Each group tracks its own position, called an offset, for each partition. Workers within a group share the partitions. Committing an offset records progress; it does not delete the event.

outcomes.reason: Six criteria supported: API producer/broker/worker trace, confirmed configured handoff before acceptance, saved render/result before ready and later consumer ack, pending/ready/failed status, synchronous authorization dependency and tracking cost.

All five criteria supported: missing acknowledgement permits redelivery, early acknowledgement risks lost credit, stable operation ID persists across attempts, unique marker and effect commit atomically, and idempotent database effect is not universal exactly-once delivery.

Uses increasing delayed retries with finite budget for transient outage, immediate isolation for known invalid input, visible failed/DLQ path for exhaustion, continued healthy work, and corrected cause plus prior-effect check before replay. Exact numerical retry policy is not required; all five criteria are taught.

Transfers address race to final wrong quantity 5; distinguishes delivery from completion, serializes same-item effects through retries/dead-letter resolution while allowing independent items, and names hot-item bottleneck. All five criteria supported.

Computes 40 pending jobs/second, connects oldest age to delayed completion, bounds saturated image-store concurrency, gives visible throttle/reject/defer admission, states finite storage/retention and sustained overload, and conditions worker scaling on spare downstream capacity. All six criteria supported.

Explains divided queue jobs and possible redelivery versus independent billing/analytics groups with shared within-group partitions; per-group/per-partition offsets do not delete records. One-day replay requires retained events; ordering remains partition-local and external effects need separate duplicate safety. All six criteria and exact quotes checked.

sourceChecks.claim: Azure async pattern supports accepted response, status endpoint and later result/failure; lesson correctly requires saved result before ready and does not claim work itself is faster.
RabbitMQ explicitly separates publisher confirms and consumer acknowledgements, with configured persistence and automatic requeueing on connection loss. Diagram preserves these distinct boundaries.

AWS primary article body is accessible despite its generic extracted title; it requires a client request identifier and atomic recording of that identifier with mutations. Unique transactional processed-job design instantiates that requirement; external effects remain excluded.

Azure retry supports transient/permanent distinction, increasing delays, finite attempts and idempotency. Checked competing-consumer/load-leveling sources supply poison-message isolation and deliberate resubmission after fixing cause.

Competing-consumer page warns ordering is not generally guaranteed and links ordered sessions. The stated concurrent completion counterexample is valid; serializing per-entity effects including retries resolves that specific dependency, at a hot-entity cost.

Load-leveling page explicitly warns producer rate above consumer rate grows queue/latency, aggregate downstream concurrency must be bounded, and producer shedding plus finite retention/durability limits matter. Arithmetic is correct.

Kafka 4.1 design verifies ordered partitions, per-group consumer positions, rewind and retention, plus external-output coordination limits for exactly-once. The diagram assumes the same event history for independent groups, not all workers each receiving every job.

Async pattern supports deferred work with observable results only when the caller can proceed; synchronous authorization is a logical dependency example. Broker/worker/status/retry/backlog costs follow the checked mechanisms.
